approach: The drain already continues past all eight self-stopping ends, so no production behavior changes. Evidence in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: `attempts` (1943-2056) returns Paused, Awaiting, Flagged, Failed, NeedsAccepting, Held, Skipped and Waiting at 1964, 1970, 1985-1986, 2000, 2029, 2043, 2046 and 2050-2053. `finish` (2684-2780) only calls `pass_over` for them, and `take_until_done` (2783-2799) leaves its loop only when `stopped()` is true. Run-ending arms are Budget, JobLimit and Stop (`set_stop` at 2741, 2745 and 2749), and the Failed arm's `StopCause` check (2729-2734) stays as it is. What is missing is one list and a test per state. Plan: (1) in drain.rs a macro, `item_end_kinds!`, defines a pub fieldless `ItemEndKind` and `ItemEndKind::ALL` from one list. An exhaustive `ItemEndKind::after()` (no wildcard arm) says `Continues` or `EndsRun(Option<Stop>)`, and an exhaustive `ItemEnd::kind()` ties the private enum to it. (2) `finish` takes the three run-ending stops from `after()`, after its `pass_over` as before. (3) A unit test in drain.rs calls `finish` for a sample of every kind and checks the stop against an independent table. (4) tests/drain.rs gets four stub knobs (`held_runs`, `unread`, `waiting_to_merge`, `hold_on_retry`), eight `the_batch_goes_on_past_*` tests through `drain::drain`, two limit tests after a skipped item, one Idle test, and an exhaustiveness test mapping every kind to the test that drives it. Round-2 fixes: Paused and Awaiting are driven through `attempts` (second failure, drain.rs:2043 and 2051), not through the planning-time hold in `prepare` (2238-2258), which never dispatches the item. Idle is driven by a usage-limit run. Every new scenario carries complete plan entries so no planning read happens. The state and reason stay on the live `plan       <id> passed over: <reason>` line; `display::drain`'s end summary lists the item only under `queued` and is not changed. No refusal or matching rule is added, so no refusal_corpus case applies.

decisions.choice: One list: a macro `item_end_kinds!` in drain.rs defines the pub fieldless enum `ItemEndKind` and `ItemEndKind::ALL: &'static [ItemEndKind]` from a single invocation of 13 names (Landed, Failed, Budget, JobLimit, Stop, Idle, NeedsAccepting, Held, Skipped, Waiting, Paused, Flagged, Awaiting). `pub enum AfterItem { Continues, EndsRun(Option<Stop>) }` and `ItemEndKind::after()` is an exhaustive match with no wildcard arm: Budget→EndsRun(Some(BudgetSpent)), JobLimit→EndsRun(Some(JobLimit)), Stop→EndsRun(Some(Requested)), Idle→EndsRun(None) (another worker already set the stop; `run_job` returns Ended only when `st.stop.is_some()`, drain.rs:1622-1623), every other kind→Continues. `ItemEnd::kind()` is also an exhaustive match. Docs on `ItemEnd` and the module text point at the list.
decisions.reason: `ItemEnd` is private and carries `String` payloads (drain.rs:1423-1458), so the integration test in tests/drain.rs cannot name it; a pub fieldless kind is visible, as `Stop::ALL` is (used at tests/drain.rs:2500). Generating the enum and `ALL` from one macro invocation means a variant cannot be in the enum and missing from `ALL`. A new `ItemEnd` variant then breaks the build at `kind()`, a new kind breaks it at `after()`, and the test's own match breaks it in tests/drain.rs. ALL is a slice, so the macro needs no count. The macro has plain `$(#[$doc:meta])* $kind:ident,` arms.

rejected.option: A hand-written `const ALL` array beside the enum, like `Stop::ALL` (drain.rs:1091)
rejected.why: A variant missing from the array is silent, and the request asks that adding a state without handling it fails.
It is private to drain.rs, and tests/drain.rs is an integration test that sees only pub items.

rejected.option: A derive crate such as strum
rejected.why: It adds a dependency, and D173 requires a decision for each new one.

rejected.option: Have the macro also generate the `after()` match from `Kind => Class` pairs
rejected.why: The match would be invisible in the diff, and the criterion asks the diff to show no wildcard arm.

decisions.choice: `Drain::finish` takes the three run-ending stops from the list. It computes `let after = end.kind().after();` before the match, keeps each arm's `pass_over` call, drops the three `self.set_stop(..)` calls in the Budget, JobLimit and Stop arms, and after the match runs `if let AfterItem::EndsRun(Some(stop)) = after { self.set_stop(stop); }`. The Landed arm and the Failed arm's `StopCause` check (2729-2734) are not edited. A comment says Landed returns early and takes its stops from rating and rebuild.
decisions.reason: The list is then the code, not a second description of it. Order is as before (the line is printed, then the stop is set), so a parallel worker never sees the stop before the line. `set_stop` keeps the first reason (1587-1592), so another worker's earlier stop still wins. Failed is `Continues` because the environment stop is a cause-of-failure rule, not an item-state rule; sorting failures by cause is out of scope.

rejected.option: Leave `finish` alone and only check it against the list in a test
rejected.why: The list could then drift from the code between tests; using it makes it authoritative.

rejected.option: A `debug_assert!` in `finish` that a Continues kind leaves `stop` unset
rejected.why: With parallel workers another worker may set a stop between the two reads, so the assert would be flaky.

rejected.option: Mark Failed as EndsRun when its cause is environmental
rejected.why: That is failure-cause sorting, which the brief puts out of scope.

decisions.choice: The state and reason stay on the existing live line `plan       <id> passed over: <reason>` (`pass_over`, drain.rs:1542-1550, once per item per run). `Report` and `display::drain` are not changed. D190 and the CHANGELOG say so plainly: the state and reason are on that line, and the end summary (`display::drain`, display.rs:767-895) shows the item only under `queued`. Each reason names its state: 'line a is paused', 'line a is flagged', 'awaiting diagnosis', 'failed twice', 'held:', 'not ready:', 'skipped:', 'waiting to merge' (finish 2715-2778; paused and flagged texts from the scope guard).
decisions.reason: The accepted reading names the pass-over line as the summary entry, and the change is sized as one list plus tests. Round-1 finding 3 is accepted: the existing assertions do not forbid a summary list. tests/drain.rs:814 counts only summary lines holding both 'line a is paused' and 'lift', and 1062-1063 forbid only 'repeated failure' and 'failed twice' for a flagged item. So a summary list is possible, and the plan declines it for size and for the reading, not because those tests would break.

rejected.option: Add a passed-over list to `Report` and the end summary
rejected.why: It changes `Report` JSON and display output beyond the accepted reading, and the live line already carries job, state and reason.

decisions.choice: Paused and Awaiting are driven through `attempts`, not through the planning-time hold. Paused: the existing knob `pause_on_retry: Some(("a", pause_text("a")))` with outcomes Rejected, Rejected, Landed; the stub pushes the pause when `a-retry` runs (tests/drain.rs:234-240), so the second failure reaches `paused_reason` at drain.rs:2042-2043 (ItemEnd::Paused). Awaiting: a new knob `hold_on_retry: Option<(&'static str, &'static str)>` plus `held_now: RefCell<Vec<(String,String)>>`, filled when `<item>-retry` runs, and a new `Steps::held` override that returns `held_now` filtered by the jobs asked about. The hold check at the top of the second attempt (1969) finds nothing, the retry runs, and the second failure reaches `held_reason` at 2050-2051 (ItemEnd::Awaiting). Flagged and Failed already reach 2046 and 2052 through `outcomes` Rejected, Rejected, Landed.
decisions.reason: Answers round-1 finding 1. Read from code: `prepare` asks `steps.paused(&ids)` and `steps.held(&ids)` for the whole queue before any dispatch (2238-2251), skips those items (2258) and stores them in `pause_held` (2325, 2416); `pass_over_paused` prints their one line (2451-2458, called at 3146 and 3212). An item configured with `paused: [("a", ..)]` is never dispatched (the existing test asserts the log is only read b, run b, land b, rate, tests/drain.rs:796-802), so `ItemEnd::Paused`/`Awaiting` and the `finish` arm at 2769-2771 are not reached. A test on that path would still pass if the arm were mutated to stop the run. With the retry-time knobs the arm is reached. The planning-time hold stays covered by the existing tests at 787-867 and 9899-10082, which are not edited.

rejected.option: Configure `paused` and `held` from the start (planning-time hold)
rejected.why: The item is never dispatched, so the `finish` arm under test is never reached and criterion 5 would go unshown.

rejected.option: Add a second planning-time Awaiting test as well
rejected.why: The existing real-steps tests at tests/drain.rs:9927-10045 already cover it; the request is one change, kept small.

decisions.choice: Exhaustiveness test `every_end_of_an_item_has_a_test_that_drives_it` in tests/drain.rs. For each kind in `ItemEndKind::ALL`, a match with no wildcard arm returns the name of the driving test: Landed→`a_rating_is_never_taken_before_a_landing` (1520; asserts a lands and is rated and c lands after b's failed landing), Failed→`the_batch_goes_on_past_an_item_that_failed_twice`, Budget→`the_batch_goes_on_past_a_skipped_item_only_while_budget_remains`, JobLimit→`the_batch_goes_on_past_a_skipped_item_only_while_slots_remain`, Stop→`a_stop_asked_for_mid_run_finishes_the_current_job_and_starts_no_other` (1382; ItemEnd::Stop is reached for b because the stop is requested while a runs), Idle→`an_item_that_finds_the_run_already_ended_is_passed_over_and_nothing_else_starts` (new), NeedsAccepting, Held, Skipped, Waiting, Paused, Flagged and Awaiting→their `the_batch_goes_on_past_*` tests. It asserts `include_str!("drain.rs")` contains `#[test]\nfn <name>(`, and that every kind whose `after()` is `Continues`, except Landed, maps to a name starting `the_batch_goes_on_past_`.
decisions.reason: A new variant fails to compile at the match; a deleted or renamed driving test fails at run time and names the kind. Idle is mapped to a new test because the round-1 mapping was wrong: c's 'run ended first' line in `passed_over_item_is_logged_once_with_its_reason` (6635-6670) comes from `sweep` (drain.rs:2497, 2503), not from the Idle arm (2751-2753). Idle arises in a serial run when an item's first job hits a usage limit: `stop_for_usage_limit` (1779) sets the stop, the retry's `run_job` returns Ended (1622-1623) and `attempts` returns Idle (1984). The existing usage-limit test (1227) asserts only the stop and the log and prints through a Stamped ui it never reads, so it cannot be the mapping; the new test asserts the Idle line.

rejected.why: It does not name which kind lacks a test and breaks on every legitimate addition.

rejected.option: Map Idle to the existing usage-limit test (1227)
rejected.why: It never asserts the Idle pass-over line, so deleting the Idle arm would not fail it.

decisions.choice: Every new stub scenario carries complete plan entries `planned("a", Ladder::Implementation, &["src/a.rs"], &[])`, `b` and (for the limit tests) `c`, as the existing pass-over tests do (tests/drain.rs:792-795). Budget and job-limit values come from the arithmetic below. Stub costs: read 0.1, run 0.5, rate 0.2; caps read 0.2, run 1.0, rate 0.3 (tests/drain.rs:39, 128-134); `Budget::fits` is spent + held + cap ≤ total (drain.rs:366-368).
decisions.reason: Answers round-1 finding 4. `prepare` reads an item at planning only when its plan entry exists and is incomplete (drain.rs:2265-2289); a read error there becomes a forced refusal, 'the request could not be read' (2299-2305), not `RunStep::Unread`/`ItemEnd::Skipped`, and the planning read also adds to the budget (2292). Complete entries make `missing().is_empty()` true, so the loop continues at 2269 and no planning read happens. Job-limit test: max_jobs 3; a's two reads start 2 jobs (`started += 1` per `run_job`, 1631), b starts the third and lands, c finds `started >= max_jobs` (1625) → ItemEnd::JobLimit. Budget test: a's two reads spend 0.2; b spends 0.1+0.5 then 0.2 for its rating, total 1.0; a's second read needs 0.1+1.2 ≤ X, b's read needs 0.2+1.2 ≤ X, so X ≥ 1.4, and c's read+run reserve fails when 1.0+1.2 > X, so X < 2.2. The test uses 2.0, which sits in [1.4, 2.2) with 0.2 of margin to the upper bound and 0.6 to the lower (float slack is 1e-9). The producer confirms it by running the test.

rejected.option: Plan entries left out (items with no plan entry)
rejected.why: It also avoids a planning read, but then the order and grouping come from the no-plan path and differ from the existing pass-over tests; complete entries match them.

decisions.choice: Exit table of `Drain::attempts` and `Drain::finish`. The next reader is `take_until_done` (2783-2799: `stopped()`, then `pop_front`), the one caller of `work` and `finish` (2794, 2797), and the report (`queued`, `jobs`, `stop`). Landed: attempts 2024-2027, finish 2686-2714; leaves the item landed and then a rebuild and rating, whose stops `stopped()` reads next; list says Continues. Failed: attempts 2050-2053, finish 2715-2735; leaves the item queued with a 'failed twice' line, and sets Stop::Environment only for ProducerAuth or LowDisk; list says Continues. Budget: attempts 1982, 2031 (landing re-check) and 1715 (no room for the run, which returns RunStep::Budget); finish 2736-2742; line, then BudgetSpent from the list; `stopped()` ends the loop. JobLimit: attempts 1983; finish 2743-2746; line, then JobLimit from the list. Stop (interrupt): attempts 1958-1959; finish 2747-2750; line, then Requested from the list. Idle: attempts 1984; finish 2751-2753; line only, the stop was set by another worker or a usage limit, `stopped()` already true. NeedsAccepting: attempts 1985; finish 2754-2760; line 'not ready:', no stop, item stays queued. Held: attempts 1986; finish 2761-2767; line 'held:', no stop. Waiting: attempts 2029; finish 2768; line 'waiting to merge', no stop. Paused: attempts 1964 and 2043; Flagged: 2046; Awaiting: 1970 and 2051; all finish 2769-2771; line with the scope guard's reason, no stop. Skipped: attempts 1987-2000 (unread twice); finish 2772-2778; line 'skipped:', no stop. Error exits: a read with an error and a job lands in Unread→Skipped (1692-1702); a read with no job, and a run with no outcome, land in Failed after two attempts (1704, 1772-1792). A usage limit sets the stop at 1779 and the next `run_job` returns Idle. `queue()` failing after a wave notes and breaks (3214-3219) and is unchanged. A worker panic is not changed by this plan.
decisions.reason: Only the three `set_stop` arms of `finish` change, and they now read the same values from the list in the same order (line, then stop). Every other arm keeps its text; `attempts` is not edited.

risks.risk: The request reads as if the drain stops today, but the code already continues for all eight states, so a reader may expect a behavior change.
risks.mitigation: State plainly in the CHANGELOG and D190 that the drain already continued past each state (drain.rs:1964-2053 and 2684-2778) and that the change adds the one list, its checks and the tests. The producer must not invent a behavior change.

risks.risk: 'Its summary' may be read as the end-of-run summary, which this plan does not change.
risks.mitigation: Say in D190 and the CHANGELOG that state and reason are on the live passed-over line and that the end summary lists the item only under `queued`. The accepted reading names the pass-over line, and the plan does not claim existing tests forbid a summary list.

risks.risk: The budget-limit value depends on the stub costs and caps and on `Budget::fits`, so a wrong constant would make the test pass or fail for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: The budget test uses 2.0, with the range 1.4 ≤ X < 2.2 derived in the decisions and a comment in the test showing the sum. The producer confirms it by running the test and keeps `assert_eq!(report.stop, Stop::BudgetSpent)` exact. The job-limit test is deterministic.

risks.risk: The verifier has no command that edits the tree, so criterion 5's mutation check cannot be re-run by it.
risks.mitigation: The producer applies the arm mutations itself, runs the `the_batch_goes_on_past_` tests, names the failing test and assertion for each, and reverts all of them; the report says so. The verifier checks the assertions by reading the diff.

risks.risk: The macro could trip clippy or make the list harder to grep.
risks.mitigation: Use plain `$(#[$doc:meta])* $kind:ident,` arms, docs on the generated items, an `#[allow]` only if clippy asks, and run clippy with `-D warnings` before finishing. A macro is rare in this repository (athena-agent/src/policy.rs:189, athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:527), so the producer keeps it to one small `macro_rules!`.

risks.risk: Calling `finish(Landed)` in the unit test runs `rebuild_if_due` and `rate`, which could set a stop and confuse the agreement check.
risks.mitigation: The unit test uses `target_rating: 4` against the stub's rating of 3 and a 9.0 budget, so `rate()` sets no stop; Landed is checked in the same loop as the other kinds, and a comment says why. Before this check the producer reads `rate()` (2520-2602) to confirm.

risks.risk: A race in the stamped run counts if a new test ran with parallel workers.
risks.mitigation: The new tests use `drain::drain`, which is serial (`run_serial`, 2821), so the order of lines and log entries is deterministic. The parallel module tests are not edited.

risks.risk: The D187 gate checks new statement-opening phrases in docs/decisions.md for links no one adds, and another job may have taken D190.
risks.mitigation: D190 avoids those phrases; the producer runs the decision-log check through `cargo test --locked` and reports any link demand, since docs/decision-links.toml is not a deliverable. The producer also confirms that D190 is the next free number at the end of docs/decisions.md before writing it.

demonstrations.method: Read `git diff crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs` for: the `item_end_kinds!` invocation listing all 13 kinds; `ItemEndKind::after()` and `ItemEnd::kind()`, each a match with no `_ =>` arm; and `finish` calling `end.kind().after()` and setting the stop from it. Then run the unit test in the `tests` module (drain.rs:4964), which holds `sample(kind) -> ItemEnd` (an exhaustive match, no wildcard) and a separate `expected_stop(kind)` table written as literals.
demonstrations.observes: The list covers Landed, Failed, Budget, JobLimit, Stop, Idle, NeedsAccepting, Held, Skipped, Waiting, Paused, Flagged and Awaiting. For every kind in `ALL`, `sample(kind).kind() == kind`; `ALL` has no repeated kind; and after `Drain::new(&stub, &Quiet, caps, Limits{budget_usd: 9.0, target_rating: 4, max_jobs: 10})` and `d.finish(&Item::queued("j1", "t"), sample(kind))`, `d.st().stop` equals `expected_stop(kind)` (BudgetSpent, JobLimit and Requested for the three; none for the rest, Landed included because the stub rates 3 against the target 4) and `kind.after()` agrees with it.
demonstrations.seam: Existing: `Drain::new` and `Drain::finish` (drain.rs:2606, 2684), reached from the `tests` module because it is a child of the module; `tests::Stub` (4970) already implements `Steps` and is the injected steps. Step 4 adds `sample` and `expected_stop` (both exhaustive matches) and the test. The stub only returns scripted values; the stop decision under test is the production `finish`.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of tests/drain.rs for the match over `ItemEndKind` with no wildcard arm that names one driving test per kind, then run the test. A deleted or renamed driving test fails the run and names its kind.

demonstrations.method: Eight tests, one per continuing state, each building a Stub of items a and b with complete plan entries and driving a into one state, all through `drain::drain(&stub, limits(9.0), &ui)` with the `Stamped` ui (tests/drain.rs:743-777). Paused: outcomes Rejected, Rejected, Landed, `pause_on_retry: Some(("a", pause_text("a")))` (attempts, drain.rs:2043). Flagged: the same outcomes, `flagged: [("a", flag_text("a"))]` (2046). Awaiting: the same outcomes, new `hold_on_retry: Some(("a", hold_text("a")))` (2051). Failed twice: the same outcomes, no pause or flag (2052). Held: new `held_runs: ["a"]`, so `run` returns `held: true` with reason 'budget short: ...' (1745-1770). Needs accepting: existing `needs_accepting: ["a"]` (1733-1743). Skipped: new `unread: ["a"]`, so both reads of a return a job and an error (1692-1702, 1994-2000). Waiting: new `waiting_to_merge: ["a"]`, so `land` returns `Landing::Waiting` (1919-1924, 2029). A shared helper `assert_batch_continues(kind, stub, state, reason)` asserts: `kind.after() == AfterItem::Continues`; exactly one line starting `plan       a passed over:` that contains the state text and the reason text; that line was stamped after a's own runs and before b's (its run count equals the number of log entries starting `run a`); `report.jobs` holds b with outcome 'passed' and landing 'landed'; the log holds `run b` then `land b`; `report.landed == 1`; `report.stop == Stop::QueueEmpty`; a is still in `report.queued`; and `display::drain` contains 'stopped     queue empty'.
demonstrations.observes: Each state yields one pass-over line with job a, the state words ('is paused', 'is flagged', 'awaiting diagnosis', 'failed twice', 'held:', 'not ready:', 'skipped:', 'waiting to merge') and the reason, then b runs and lands, and the run ends queue-empty.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the `finish` arm for a state called `set_stop`, or `attempts` returned a run-ending end for it, b would not run: `stub.log()` would lack `run b` and `land b`, b's job line would not read passed and landed, `report.landed` would be 0 and `report.stop` would not be QueueEmpty, so the test fails. Printing the pass-over line alone is not enough to pass.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point: `athena_cli::drain::drain` (drain.rs:3021). Guards: `stop_requested` (1958), `paused_reason` (1963, 2042), `held_reason` (1969, 2050), the job-limit and budget checks (1625-1630) and `ATTEMPTS` (2036). Fixture: `Stub` in tests/drain.rs, injected as the `&dyn Steps`; it exists today for Paused, Flagged, Failed and NeedsAccepting (`pause_on_retry`, `flagged`, `outcomes`, `needs_accepting`). Step 5 adds `held_runs`, `unread`, `waiting_to_merge`, `hold_on_retry` with `held_now` and the `Steps::held` override, plus their branches in `read`, `run` and `land`, all empty by default. The stub returns scripted inputs only; the continue-or-stop logic under test is the production `Drain`.

demonstrations.method: Two tests, items a, b, c with complete plan entries, `unread: ["a"]`, `outcomes: passing()`, `ratings: [1]`. (i) `the_batch_goes_on_past_a_skipped_item_only_while_slots_remain`: `Limits { max_jobs: 3, ..limits(9.0) }`. a spends 2 job slots on its two reads, b takes the third and lands, and c finds no slot (drain.rs:1625). Assert `report.stop == Stop::JobLimit`, `report.landed == 1`, the log is `read a`, `read a`, `read b`, `run b`, `land b`, `rate`, one line `plan       a passed over: skipped: ...`, one line `plan       c passed over: over the job limit`, and `ItemEndKind::JobLimit.after() == AfterItem::EndsRun(Some(Stop::JobLimit))`. (ii) `the_batch_goes_on_past_a_skipped_item_only_while_budget_remains`: `limits(2.0)`, chosen from 1.4 ≤ X < 2.2 (a's two reads and b's read, run and rating spend 1.0; c needs 1.2 more); a comment in the test shows the sum, and the producer confirms the value by running the test. Assert `report.stop == Stop::BudgetSpent`, `report.landed == 1`, the log has `rate` after `land b` and no `read c`, a has its 'skipped:' line, and c has one pass-over line.
demonstrations.observes: The skipped item is passed over, b lands, and the run then ends with the Stop reason of the exhausted slot or budget; c is never read.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the drain ignored its limits after a pass-over, c would be read and run and `report.stop` would not be JobLimit or BudgetSpent, so the stop assertions and the absence of `read c` in the log would fail. If the pass-over of a stopped the run, b would not land and `report.landed` would not be 1.
demonstrations.seam: Production: `drain::drain` with `Limits { max_jobs, budget_usd, target_rating }` (`Limits` is imported at tests/drain.rs:13; `limits()` at 332). Guards: `run_job` checks at drain.rs:1622-1630 and the finish arms for Budget (2736-2742) and JobLimit (2743-2746). Fixture: `Stub` with the new `unread` knob (step 5); caps are the stub's 0.2, 1.0 and 0.3 (128-134). The tests are added by step 7.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff to confirm each of the eight tests asserts the later item's landing in `report.jobs`, in `stub.log()` and in `report.landed`, and not only that a line was printed. The verifier has no command that edits the tree, so the mutation check is the producer's, reported in its output: it changes the arm `ItemEnd::Paused(reason) | ItemEnd::Flagged(reason) | ItemEnd::Awaiting(reason)` in `finish` (2769-2771) to also call `self.set_stop(Stop::Requested)`, runs `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain the_batch_goes_on_past_`, and reports that the Paused, Flagged and Awaiting tests fail on the b-landed and QueueEmpty assertions. It does the same for the Held, NeedsAccepting, Skipped, Waiting and Failed arms, names the failing test each time, and reverts every mutation before it ends.
demonstrations.observes: The tests fail when the pass-over of that state ends the run, and pass on the real tree.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the pass-over of a state stopped the run, the assertions that b's job line is 'passed' and 'landed', that `land b` is in the log, that `report.landed == 1` and that `report.stop == QueueEmpty` all fail, as does the `finish_agrees_with_the_item_end_list` unit test's stop check. The Paused, Flagged and Awaiting tests fail in particular, because each reaches `ItemEnd::Paused`, `Flagged` or `Awaiting` through `attempts` (drain.rs:2043, 2046, 2051) and not the planning-time hold.
demonstrations.seam: Same as criterion 3. The mutation is on the production `Drain::finish`, never committed. The unit test's `expected_stop` table is a separate literal from `after()`, so a change to either is seen.
